kernel_modules.manifest_method: SHA-256 of the sorted regular-file relative-path SHA-256 manifest; validated input and donor build/source symlinks are stripped from the package

runtime_constraints: The service requires root and a root-owned mode-0700 ramfs or tmpfs runtime directory.
The supplicant control directory and socket must be root-controlled.
Lease input is validated before fixed BusyBox commands are executed without a shell.
A full-lifetime lock prevents concurrent supervisors.
Prior non-child process records are never used to signal a PID on the target's pre-pidfd kernel.
DHCP event handlers must match the active owner token and interface before changing network state.
All lease, resolver, lock, PID, and ownership state remains in RAM.
validation: Two clean static ARMv7 builds were byte-identical.
Owned DHCP acquired a lease and preserved gateway, public IPv4, and DNS reachability.
Graceful shutdown removed DHCP, IPv4, route, resolver, and lease state.
Station disconnect cleaned state and reconnect reacquired connectivity.
A second supervisor was rejected without disturbing the active service.
A reused stale PID was ignored without signaling the unrelated process, and supervision reacquired connectivity.
A disowned DHCP event left the active route and failure marker unchanged.
Authenticated credential replacement stopped the prior supplicant and DHCP child, then the unchanged supervisor reacquired association, lease, route, resolver, IPv4, and DNS.
Two packaged initramfs builds were byte-identical and contained the reviewed daemon, adapters, release manifest, and PID 1.
Checksum-gated image cold-booted in yellow mode at 2026-09-03T17:36Z; PID 1 auto-started networkd, the RAM-only root remained unmounted from NAND, and the SD8887 WLAN/Bluetooth drivers loaded.

Cold-boot networkd correctly waited for a root-controlled station supplicant; no station credentials were included in this image, so association, DHCP, DNS, and route acquisition were not expected or attempted.
